executive_summary:
L&Q has reported a first-quarter deficit after booking a £233m loss on the sale of its private rented sector business, though the housing association says the disposal has let it cut debt. The scale of the write-down underlines how exposed even top-tier registered providers have been to PRS portfolio repricing.

Inside Housing reports that Vivid is exploring taking a stake in a house builder, a move that would mark a further step by large associations into direct development capacity rather than relying solely on Section 106 and forward-funded pipelines. No terms or target have been disclosed.

Birmingham City Council has publicly criticised GreenSquareAccord for declining to complete a sale of a development to a local co-operative at the price originally agreed, blaming construction cost and interest rate inflation. The row is a visible symptom of how build cost escalation is straining delivery partnerships between local authorities, associations and community groups.

National house price data continues to soften: growth has slowed to its weakest pace since 2023 with the average property value effectively flat at £299,253, while commentary around the October Budget is reportedly already dampening transaction sentiment. In London, the salary needed to buy the average property has risen 6.4% to £74,520 as rents climb 4.2%, reinforcing the affordability gap that continues to support rental demand.

Local planning activity remains active at the margins, with Preston City Council approving conversion of the Miller Arcade into 46 flats and Pendle Council clearing an M&S foodhall scheme near Colne, but these are small, single-site items against a subdued macro backdrop.

sentiment.rationale: National price growth is at its weakest since 2023 and agents are citing Budget-related tax speculation and mortgage conditions as depressing activity, while a major association has taken a large loss tied to PRS disposal; the only clearly positive signals are isolated strategic moves by housing associations rather than a broad market improvement.
